text: Rough, narrow Forest Service spur roads with a documented history of washouts, downed trees, blown culverts, and sinkholes on this section of the Skykomish Ranger District. The Forest Service's Skykomish District road-damage alert of June 30, 2026 lists FR 6510 (Bolt Creek Road) closed at its gate at milepost 1.0, with a blown-out culvert at MP 1.2 and a bridge out at MP 2, and FR 6514 (Eagle Creek Road) gated closed at milepost 0, with a blown culvert at MP 1.6 and a sinkhole at MP 7.1; no reopening date is given, so no vehicle can reach this trailhead while that stands. Skykomish Ranger District: (360) 677-2414.

Closed to vehicles: the Forest Service's Skykomish District road-damage alert of June 30, 2026 lists FR 6514 (Eagle Creek Road), which the NF-6514-410 spur to this trailhead leaves, gated closed at milepost 0 with a blown culvert at MP 1.6, and FR 6510 (Bolt Creek Road) closed at its gate at milepost 1.0; no reopening date is given. Skykomish Ranger District: (360) 677-2414.

Index-Galena Road (FR 63) has been closed to vehicles between mileposts 10 and 14 since December 2025 flood damage, with no repair timeline. The Beckler Road/Jack Pass detour is closed too: since June 30, 2026 the Forest Service lists FR 65 as graded only to Jack Pass (milepost 12.3) and closed beyond it for downed trees and a bridge out, and FR 63 as undrivable from the FR 65 side because the North Fork Skykomish bridge is out, so no vehicle route currently reaches the Blanca Lake Trailhead. Check with Snohomish County Public Works and the Skykomish Ranger District, (360) 677-2414, before you go.

From US-2 near Index, FR 63 runs north along the North Fork Skykomish River, but it has been closed to vehicles between mileposts 10 and 14 since December 2025 flood damage, with no repair timeline on Snohomish County's road-closures page as of September 25, 2026. When open, the detour is US-2 to Beckler Road (FR 65) near Skykomish, ~12.5 mi to Jack Pass, then ~1.8–2.5 mi on FR 63 to the Blanca Lake Trailhead — gravel, rough in spots, roughly 45 minutes longer than the old Index route; low-clearance cars and RVs can struggle.

White River Road typically open early July–September; Carbon River/Ipsut Creek access has been closed at SR-165's Fairfax Bridge since April 22, 2025, to vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians, with no end date given as of the Mount Rainier National Park road-status page updated September 18, 2026
Anderson-Watson Road 1107 has been closed by a washout at mile 3.8 since July 2026, with no reopening date, so the Watson Lakes trailhead is roughly 6 miles farther up the road.

From Darrington, drive Highway 530 to the Suiattle River Road (Forest Road 26) and turn east; the trailhead is in a parking lot just past the Downey Creek bridge, about 20 miles from Highway 530. Since February 2026 the road has been closed to vehicles at milepost 4 (order in place to January 2028), so the last miles must be covered on foot or by bike.

From SR 20 near milepost 82, turn north onto Baker Lake Road (Forest Road 11) and go about 14 miles, turn right onto Baker Dam Road and cross Upper Baker Dam, then turn left onto FR 1107 and follow it about 8.9 miles to the Anderson and Watson Lakes junction and 1.1 miles more to the trailhead. A washout has closed FR 1107 to vehicles since July 2026.

From Acme on WA-9, turn east onto Mosquito Lake Road and follow it about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River and continue onto Forest Road 38 for about 11 miles to the Elbow Lake trailhead. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.

From Index on US-2, turn north onto Index-Galena Road (FR-63) and drive about 16 miles, bearing left at the junction for the final 2 miles of bumpy gravel. Bear left again at the second fork and climb a short hill to the parking area. Flood damage has closed Index-Galena Road between about milepost 10 and milepost 14 since December 2025 with no repair date, and Beckler River Road (FR-65) is closed as well, so the trailhead cannot be reached by car right now.

From SR-542 about 3 miles east of Deming, turn right onto Mosquito Lake Road, go 4.8 miles, then turn left onto Middle Fork Road (FR-38) and follow it about 12.3 miles to where the road begins switchbacking uphill; park there, or sooner if snow stops you. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.

The highway is gated here for the season and has been closed beyond since October 25, 2026, so this is where cars stop in winter; in summer the road continues to the Artist Point lot.
